entry: American film director and producer. He is known for big-budget action films with fast cutting, stylized cinematography and extensive special effects, including frequent explosions. His films include *Bad Boys* (1995), *The Rock* (1996), *Armageddon* (1998), *Pearl Harbor* (2001) and the first five films of the [[Transformers]] series. *Armageddon* and *Pearl Harbor* each received four Academy Award nominations. His films have grossed over US$6.6 billion worldwide. Critics have faulted his preference for spectacle over story and character, and his use of racial stereotypes for comic effect.

American businessman and politician, founder of Bloomberg L.P., a financial information and media firm known for the Bloomberg Terminal. He was the 109th mayor of New York City from 2002 to 2013. As mayor he established public charter schools, rebuilt urban infrastructure, and supported gun control and public health initiatives. He led a re-zoning that facilitated new construction after the [[September 11 attacks]], and he faced significant criticism for the city's stop-and-frisk program. He self-funded $935 million for his 2020 campaign for the Democratic presidential nomination, the most expensive presidential primary campaign in U.S. history. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2024.

English retired actor known for his distinctive Cockney accent. Breakthrough roles in the 1960s included *Zulu* (1964), *The Ipcress File* (1965) and *The Italian Job* (1969), and he appeared in more than 130 films over a career spanning eight decades. He won two [[Academy Awards]] for best supporting actor, for *Hannah and Her Sisters* (1986) and *The Cider House Rules* (1999). He played Alfred Pennyworth in the [[Batman]] trilogy directed by [[Christopher Nolan]]. He was knighted by [[Elizabeth II]] in 2000. His final film was *The Great Escaper* (2023).

Irish revolutionary, soldier and politician. Born in County Cork, Collins moved to London in 1906 and became associated there with the Irish Republican Brotherhood. He fought in the [[Easter Rising]] of 1916 and was held as a prisoner of war. During the [[Irish War of Independence]] he was Director of Intelligence of the Irish Republican Army (IRA) and planned attacks on British forces, including the assassinations of British intelligence agents on "Bloody Sunday" in November 1920. He was one of the delegates who negotiated the Anglo-Irish Treaty in London. The treaty established the Irish Free State but required an oath of allegiance to the Crown, and republicans including De Valera opposed that clause. Collins supported the treaty, chaired the provisional government in 1922 and commanded the National Army. He was shot dead in an ambush by anti-Treaty forces during the Irish Civil War.

American author and filmmaker whose novels often feature technology, biotechnology and genetic engineering. He received an MD from Harvard Medical School in 1969 but did not practice medicine. His novels include *The Andromeda Strain* (1969), *Sphere* (1987) and [[Jurassic Park]] (1990), and over a dozen have been adapted into films. He wrote and directed *Westworld* (1973), the first film to use 2D computer-generated imagery, and created the television series *ER*. His skepticism toward environmentalism, voiced in the 2003 speech "Environmentalism as Religion" and the novel *State of Fear* (2004), drew controversy.

American businessman and philanthropist. He founded Dell in 1984 while a student at the University of Texas, selling upgraded personal computers directly to consumers and building them after orders were received. In January 2013 he bid to take Dell Inc. private for $24.4 billion, the biggest management buyout since the [[Great Recession]]; the company went private that October and went public again in December 2018. He is chairman and chief executive of Dell Technologies, in which he owns a 40% stake as of 2026.

American actor and film producer. He won an Academy Award as producer of *One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest* (1975), which won Best Picture, and an Academy Award for Best Actor for playing Gordon Gekko in *Wall Street* (1987). Other films include *Fatal Attraction* (1987), *Basic Instinct* (1992) and *Traffic* (2000). He won a Primetime Emmy Award for portraying [[Liberace]] in the HBO film *Behind the Candelabra* (2013). He played Hank Pym in the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] from 2015 to 2023. He was appointed a [[United Nations]] Messenger of Peace in 1998.

German and Irish actor, racing driver and producer. He first came to prominence playing Bobby Sands in *Hunger* (2008) and won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor for *Shame* (2011). He received Academy Award nominations for *12 Years a Slave* (2013) and *Steve Jobs* (2015). He played Erik Lehnsherr, known as Magneto, in the [[X-Men]] film series. After racing in the European Le Mans Series in 2023, he returned to acting with *The Killer* (2023) and *Black Bag* (2025). He has been married to Swedish actress [[Alicia Vikander]] since 2017.

Irish-English actor. A founding member of the Royal National Theatre company under [[Laurence Olivier]], he won three Olivier Awards. He appeared in many productions of [[William Shakespeare]]'s plays, including *Othello*, *Hamlet* and *Macbeth*. He won four BAFTA TV Awards, including for *The Singing Detective* (1986). He played Albus Dumbledore in the [[Harry Potter (film series)|Harry Potter]] films from 2004 to 2011. He was knighted by [[Elizabeth II]] in 1998 for services to drama.

Canadian-American actor and activist. He played Marty McFly in the [[Back to the Future]] film trilogy (1985–1990). He played Alex P. Keaton in the NBC sitcom *Family Ties* (1982–1989) and Mike Flaherty in the ABC sitcom *Spin City*, winning Primetime Emmy Awards for both. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 1991 and disclosed it in 1998. He founded The Michael J. Fox Foundation in 2000 to help fund research toward a cure. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2025.

American former basketball player and businessman. Jordan played 15 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), mostly with the [[Chicago Bulls]], and won six NBA championships, in 1991, 1992, 1993, 1996, 1997 and 1998. He was named Most Valuable Player five times and Finals MVP six times. He holds the NBA records for career regular season scoring average (30.1 points per game) and career playoff scoring average (33.4 points per game). He retired abruptly before the 1993–94 season to play minor league baseball, then returned to the Bulls. He won four gold medals with the United States national team, including at the 1984 and 1992 Summer Olympics. He made many product endorsements and fueled the success of Nike's Air Jordan sneakers. He is a co-owner of 23XI Racing in the [[NASCAR]] Cup Series. In 2016, [[Barack Obama]] awarded him the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

American actor and filmmaker, born Eugene Maurice Orowitz. He is known for playing Little Joe Cartwright in [[Bonanza]], Charles Ingalls in *Little House on the Prairie* and Jonathan Smith in *Highway to Heaven*. He appeared on the cover of *TV Guide* 22 times, second only to [[Lucille Ball]]. He wrote, produced and directed the semi-autobiographical television movie *The Loneliest Runner*. A high school [[Javelin throw|javelin]] thrower, he earned an athletic scholarship to the University of Southern California, but torn shoulder ligaments ended his college career.

American film director, screenwriter and producer known for stylized crime dramas. He has won two Primetime Emmy Awards and earned four Academy Award nominations. He won a BAFTA Award for producing *The Aviator*. His films include *The Jericho Mile* (1979), *Thief* (1981), *Manhunter* (1986), *The Last of the Mohicans* (1992), *Heat* (1995), *The Insider* (1999), *Collateral* (2004) and *Ferrari* (2023). He was executive producer of the TV series [[Miami Vice]], which he adapted into a 2006 feature film. He became a filmmaker after seeing [[Stanley Kubrick]]'s *Dr. Strangelove*.

American former competitive swimmer. He won 28 Olympic medals across four Games, more than any other athlete, including a record 23 gold medals. At the 2004 [[Athens]] Games he won six gold and two bronze medals, tying the record of eight medals at a single Games. At the 2008 [[Beijing]] Games he won eight gold medals, breaking Mark Spitz's record of seven first-place finishes at a single Olympics. He also won four gold and two silver medals in London in 2012 and five gold and one silver in Rio de Janeiro in 2016. He held world records in five long course events. Diagnosed with [[Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder|attention deficit hyperactivity disorder]] as a child, he founded the Michael Phelps Foundation in 2008 to promote swimming and healthier lifestyles.

German former racing driver. He competed in [[Formula One]] from 1991 to 2006 and from 2010 to 2012, winning a record seven World Drivers' Championship titles, a total later tied by [[Lewis Hamilton]] in 2020. At his retirement he held the records for most wins (91), pole positions (68) and podium finishes (155), and he still holds the record for most fastest laps (77). He won his first two titles in 1994 and 1995, then five with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004. He was appointed a [[UNESCO]] Champion for Sport in 2002. In December 2013 he suffered a traumatic brain injury in a skiing accident and was placed in an induced coma for six months. He has not appeared publicly since 2014.

Archangel in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, venerated as a saint in some Christian traditions. In the earliest surviving Jewish works, from the third and second centuries BC, he is chief of the angels and guardian prince of Israel. In the [[Book of Revelation]] he battles [[Satan]], and in the Epistle of Jude he disputes with the devil over the body of [[Moses]]. Islamic tradition knows a figure called Mika'il, but the Quran does not mention him directly.

French philosopher, literary critic and historian of ideas. He analyzed the relationships among power, knowledge and liberty, and how they operate as social control through institutions. Sometimes called a structuralist or postmodernist, he rejected both labels. His work has influenced anthropology, criminology, feminism, psychology and sociology. Major books include *The History of Madness* (1961), *The Order of Things* (1966), *Discipline and Punish* (1975) and *The History of Sexuality* (1976). He taught at the Collège de France from 1970 and campaigned for prison reform and human rights. He died of complications from [[HIV/AIDS]] in Paris, the first public figure in France to die of the disease. His partner, Daniel Defert, founded the AIDES charity in his memory.

Brazilian lawyer and politician, the 37th president of Brazil from 2016 to 2019. He became president after the Senate voted 61–20 in August 2016 to remove [[Dilma Rousseff]] from office, having been acting president since May 2016. His government pursued a 20-year cap on public spending growth and a labor reform law. A 2017 poll showed 7% approval for his administration. Corruption accusations linked to the *Lava Jato* investigations were made during his term. He did not seek reelection, and [[Jair Bolsonaro]] succeeded him.

French Renaissance essayist and statesman. He popularized the essay as a literary genre, merging casual anecdote and autobiography with intellectual insight. His *Essais* (1580), expanded in later editions, influenced numerous later writers. During his lifetime he was admired more as a statesman than as an author. He served as mayor of [[Bordeaux]] from 1581 to 1585, mediating local conflicts during famine and plague. He is best known for his skeptical question, *Que sais-je?* ("What do I know?"), which reflects [[Skepticism|skepticism]] and the suspension of judgment.

Italian film director, screenwriter and editor. He is best known for the "alienation trilogy" of *L'Avventura* (1960), *La Notte* (1961) and *L'Eclisse* (1962), and for the English-language film *Blowup* (1966) and the multilingual *The Passenger* (1975). His films feature striking visual composition, subdued narratives and preoccupation with modern landscapes, and they substantially influenced later world art cinema, including the slow cinema movement. He was the first director, and one of two with Jafar Panahi, to win the Palme d'Or, Golden Lion, Golden Bear and Golden Leopard. He received Academy Award nominations for *Blowup* and an Honorary Oscar in 1995.

Hotel and restaurant guide published since 1900 by the French tire company Michelin. Originally created as a guide for French motorists, it became an international reference for dining and travel. It awards up to three Michelin stars to a select few restaurants in certain regions, based on evaluations by anonymous inspectors. The one-to-three star scale was formalized by 1931. Michelin also publishes the Green Guides, general guides to cities, regions and countries. Critics have questioned the inspectors' anonymity and the pressure that stars place on chefs.

American lawyer and writer, First Lady of the United States from 2009 to 2017. She graduated from [[Princeton University]] and Harvard Law School. She worked at the law firm Sidley Austin, where she met her future husband, [[Barack Obama]]. She later worked at the [[University of Chicago]] Medical Center. As First Lady she was an advocate for education, nutrition, physical activity and healthy eating, and the first African-American to hold the position. Her memoir *Becoming* (2018) was a bestseller. After leaving office she ranked first in the Gallup poll of the most admired woman in the United States for three straight years.

Malaysian actress. She performed her own stunts in Hong Kong action films of the 1980s and 1990s, including *Yes, Madam* (1985) and *Police Story 3: Supercop* (1992). Her international breakthrough came with *Tomorrow Never Dies* (1997), a [[James Bond]] film, and with Ang Lee's *[[Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon]]* (2000). She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for *Everything Everywhere All at Once* (2022), becoming the first Asian to win the category. In 2024 she received the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

Experiment in 1887 to detect Earth's motion through the luminiferous aether, a medium thought to carry light waves. [[Albert A. Michelson|Albert A. Michelson]] and Edward W. Morley compared the speed of light in perpendicular directions at what is now Case Western Reserve University in [[Cleveland]], Ohio. They found no significant difference, a negative result generally considered the first strong evidence against some aether theories. The experiment initiated research that led to [[Special relativity]], which rules out motion against an aether. Later experiments with greater sensitivity found no aether wind; in 2009 optical resonator experiments confirmed its absence at the 10⁻¹⁷ level.

Dutch naval officer and admiral. Born to a modest family in Zeeland, he went to sea young and became a shipmaster in the merchant fleet by the age of 30. In 1652 he entered the Dutch navy at the outbreak of the [[Anglo-Dutch wars|First Anglo-Dutch War]], rising to vice admiral. As lieutenant admiral in the Second Anglo-Dutch War he won the Four Days' Battle in 1666 and carried out the Raid on the Medway in 1667, destroying much of the English fleet and capturing the flagship *HMS Royal Charles*. In the Third Anglo-Dutch War his actions at Solebay, Schooneveld and Texel prevented an Anglo-French invasion of the Dutch coast. He was mortally wounded by cannon fire at the Battle of Augusta off [[Sicily]] while fighting the French. He received a state funeral in Amsterdam and is credited as a founder of the Netherlands Marine Corps.
